legend.rsDesc: Reputation is earned by making correct forecasts weighted by your confidence. Higher RS means more consistent accuracy.
legend.cuDesc: Confidence represents your intensity/conviction on each forecast. Correct calls increase your reputation; wrong calls decrease it.
legend.brierDesc: Lower is better. Measures calibration: (your probability − actual outcome)². Perfect score = 0.
legend.roiDesc: Average net RS change per resolved prediction. Positive = you earn RS on average; negative = you lose RS on average.
legend.truthScoreDesc: Average peer score per prediction — how consistently you beat the community consensus. Positive = you beat the crowd on average.
legend.peerScoreDesc: How much better your probability estimates are than the community consensus at the time you committed. Positive = you beat the crowd.
legend.aiScoreDesc: How much better your probability estimates are than the AI's estimate at the time you committed. Positive = you beat the AI.
legend.eloDesc: Head-to-head competitive rating. When two users commit to the same prediction, the more accurate one gains ELO from the other.
legend.glickoDesc: Skill estimate with uncertainty bounds (μ − 3σ). Accounts for how many predictions you have made — rewards consistent accuracy.
legend.weightedPeerScoreDesc: Metaculus-style time-weighted peer score. Recent predictions count more than older ones (exponential decay, half-weight every ~14 months). Positive = consistently beat the crowd.

aiLeaderboard.title: AI Panel Leaderboard
aiLeaderboard.explainer: Each AI model is scored the moment a user stakes, against the outcome — the same matched-time Brier used for humans. Lower is better; 0.25 is a coin flip.
aiLeaderboard.emptyDesc: AI-panel Brier scores appear once forecasts that were staked on resolve.
aiLeaderboard.footnote: Matched-time Brier: each model’s estimate at the instant a user staked, scored against the outcome. Members with fewer than 5 scores are hidden. The Oracle is included for comparison; “control” is a deliberately weak model — if it ties the others, the ranking isn’t meaningful yet.

sourceLeaderboard.title: Source Leaderboard
sourceLeaderboard.explainer: Byline authors and outlets scored on their own directional forecasts (author_lean), resolved against outcomes — the same accountability the user leaderboard gives predictors. Lower Brier is better; 0.25 is a coin flip.
sourceLeaderboard.author: Author
sourceLeaderboard.emptyDesc: Source scores appear once resolved predictions carry author_lean signals from their cited articles.
sourceLeaderboard.footnote: Shadow scoring: this track record is informational only and does not feed the live forecast estimate. Skill is a conservative rating (discounts low-sample noise); Brier is the raw resolved-outcome accuracy of each source's own directional lean.
